Who can address the platform at all.
Public DNS, edge firewall, allow-list, tunnels." style="rounded=1;arcSize=8;fillColor=#fde2e2;strokeColor=#9673a6;strokeWidth=2;fontSize=13;fontColor=#222222;verticalAlign=top;align=center;spacingTop=6;whiteSpace=wrap;" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="300" y="290" width="440" height="90" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="z_l1l2" value="Z0 — admission only, no zone change" style="text;html=1;align=center;fontSize=12;fontColor=#b85450;fontStyle=2;" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="300" y="385" width="440" height="18" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="l2" value="L2 — Edge gateway / routing

TLS termination, request routing, WAF.
The Z0 → Z1 trust crossing." style="rounded=1;arcSize=8;fillColor=#fde2e2;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;strokeWidth=2;fontSize=13;fontColor=#222222;verticalAlign=top;align=center;spacingTop=6;whiteSpace=wrap;" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="300" y="410" width="440" height="90" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="z_l2l3" value="→ Z1 (edge perimeter; TLS terminated)" style="text;html=1;align=center;fontSize=12;fontColor=#d6b656;fontStyle=2;" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="300" y="505" width="440" height="18" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="l3" value="L3 — Identity

Verify who the caller is. Issue tokens.
The Z1 → Z2 trust crossing." style="rounded=1;arcSize=8;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#82b366;strokeWidth=2;fontSize=13;fontColor=#222222;verticalAlign=top;align=center;spacingTop=6;whiteSpace=wrap;" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="300" y="530" width="440" height="90" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="z_l3l4" value="→ Z2 (authenticated identity verified)" style="text;html=1;align=center;fontSize=12;fontColor=#6c8ebf;fontStyle=2;" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="300" y="625" width="440" height="18" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="l4" value="L4 — Authorization

PDP decisions on (principal, action, resource).
The Z2 → Z3 trust crossing." style="rounded=1;arcSize=8;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=2;fontSize=13;fontColor=#222222;verticalAlign=top;align=center;spacingTop=6;whiteSpace=wrap;" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="300" y="650" width="440" height="90" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="z_l4l5" value="→ Z3 (authorized to proceed)" style="text;html=1;align=center;fontSize=12;fontColor=#82b366;fontStyle=2;" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="300" y="745" width="440" height="18" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="l5" value="L5 — Operational guardrails

Rate limits, quotas, kill switches, feature flags.
Gating only — no zone crossing." style="rounded=1;arcSize=8;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#b46504;strokeWidth=2;fontSize=13;fontColor=#222222;verticalAlign=top;align=center;spacingTop=6;whiteSpace=wrap;" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="300" y="770" width="440" height="90" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="z_l5l6" value="Z3 (stays within Z3; L5 gates, does not cross)" style="text;html=1;align=center;fontSize=12;fontColor=#82b366;fontStyle=2;" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="300" y="865" width="440" height="18" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="l6" value="L6 — Orchestrator / BFF

Compose downstream services. Issue the internal
identity envelope. The Z3 → Z4 trust crossing." style="rounded=1;arcSize=8;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#a45fae;strokeWidth=2;fontSize=13;fontColor=#222222;verticalAlign=top;align=center;spacingTop=6;whiteSpace=wrap;" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="300" y="890" width="440" height="90" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="z_l6l7" value="→ Z4 (envelope issued, signed per ADR-0003)" style="text;html=1;align=center;fontSize=12;fontColor=#9673a6;fontStyle=2;" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="300" y="985" width="440" height="18" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="envelope_glyph" value="🔒" style="text;html=1;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=22;fontColor=#9673a6;" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="745" y="975" width="40" height="40" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="l7" value="L7 — Service enforcement

Per-service authorization, tenant scope, audit.
Verifies the envelope on every hop within Z4." style="rounded=1;arcSize=8;fillColor=#e1d5e7;strokeColor=#d79b00;strokeWidth=2;fontSize=13;fontColor=#222222;verticalAlign=top;align=center;spacingTop=6;whiteSpace=wrap;" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="300" y="1010" width="440" height="90" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="l8" value="L8 — Semantic / agent reasoning

Whichever AI coding agent and automation runtimes
the consuming team uses (Claude, Codex, in-house, …).

Sits beside the stack. Re-enters the request path at
L1/L2 as a client — never a back-channel into L7.

<mxCell id="notes_title" value="Notes" style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=14;fontStyle=1;fontColor=#222222;" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="700" y="1190" width="640" height="22" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="notes_body" value="• Each layer box is filled with its OPERATING zone colour (the zone the layer receives). The arrow leaving the layer is labelled with the PRODUCED zone (the zone the request is in after the layer fires).

• L1 and L2 both operate in Z0 (filled red). L2 produces Z1 (TLS-terminated edge perimeter). L3 operates in Z1 (filled yellow) and produces Z2. L4 produces Z3. L5 stays in Z3 (gating only, no zone crossing). L6 produces Z4 — the envelope crossing per ADR-0003. L7 operates entirely within Z4.

• L8 sits beside the stack. Agents and automation runtimes do NOT have a back-channel into L7; they traverse the same L1 → L2 → L3 → … chain as a human user. The dashed grey arrow re-entering at L1 makes this rule visible. Per ADR-0002, agents are clients.

• The 🔒 marker on the L6 → L7 arrow is a placeholder for the workspace-specific seal stencil that will ship in Phase C.2 (full template set).

• This diagram is workspace-canonical and intentionally vendor-neutral. Profile-specific diagrams (e.g., self-hosted-vps deployment topology) belong in their own files." style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=12;fontColor=#444444;whiteSpace=wrap;" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="700" y="1214" width="640" height="240" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="footer" value="Source: architecture/control-layers.md · architecture/security-boundaries.md · ADR-0001 (eight-layer model) · ADR-0002 (agents-as-clients) · ADR-0003 (internal identity envelope)

div.div:
• Each layer box is filled with its OPERATING zone colour (the zone the layer receives). The arrow leaving the layer is labelled with the PRODUCED zone (the zone the request is in after the layer fires).
• L1 and L2 both operate in Z0 (filled red). L2 produces Z1 (TLS-terminated edge perimeter). L3 operates in Z1 (filled yellow) and produces Z2. L4 produces Z3. L5 stays in Z3 (gating only, no zone crossing). L6 produces Z4 — the envelope crossing per ADR-0003. L7 operates entirely within Z4.
• L8 sits beside the stack. Agents and automation runtimes do NOT have a back-channel into L7; they traverse the same L1 → L2 → L3 → … chain as a human user. The dashed grey arrow re-entering at L1 makes this rule visible. Per ADR-0002, agents are clients.
• The 🔒 marker on the L6 → L7 arrow is a placeholder for the workspace-specific seal stencil that will ship in Phase C.2 (full template set).
• This diagram is workspace-canonical and intentionally vendor-neutral. Profile-specific diagrams (e.g., self-hosted-vps deployment topology) belong in their own files.
